audit_notes: Model: through-thickness shear displacement of a bilayer (compliant bed under a stiff skin), xi = z/(t_bed + t_skin), primer at xi=0, surface at xi=1; the shear stress is uniform through the thickness, so du/dz = tau/G(z) with G = E/3 and a smoothed (tanh) modulus step at xi_b = t_bed/(t_bed+t_skin) = 0.875. The equation is the derivative of this strain profile; the top BC fixes the strain in the skin, and u(1) gives the areal compliance C = u(1)/tau. Analytical: C = 3*(t_bed/E_bed + t_skin/E_skin) = 3*(3.5e-4/1e5 + 5e-5/5e6) = 1.053e-8 m/Pa; sigma_c = sqrt(2w/C) = sqrt(0.1/1.053e-8) = 3.1 kPa. Baseline: uniform commercial topcoat, E = 1 MPa, 150 um (skin and bed set to 1 MPa, thicknesses 131.25 + 18.75 um): C = 4.5e-10 m/Pa, sigma_c = 14.9 kPa. Expected gain about 79 % lower release stress. Important caveat not captured by the 1D model: the stiff skin carries in-plane load and spreads the fouler's shear over a shear-lag length l = sqrt(E_skin*t_skin*t_bed/G_bed) = sqrt(5e6*5e-5*3.5e-4/3.3e4) = 1.6 mm around the 5 mm base, which enlarges the loaded bed area by about (6.6/5)^2 = 1.7 and lowers the effective compliance accordingly; sigma_c then rises by about 30 %, i.e. the real reduction is nearer 70-73 %. A thicker or stiffer skin makes this worse (l grows as sqrt(E_skin*t_skin)). Second caveat: under hull bending strain and thermal mismatch a stiff skin on a very soft bed can wrinkle when the compressive strain exceeds about 0.52*(3*E_bed/E_skin)^(2/3) = 0.52*(0.06)^(2/3) = 0.08, so wrinkling needs 8 % compressive strain, far above hull strains (<0.2 %): safe. Stress check: bed shear strain at 10 kPa is 3*1e4/1e5 = 0.3, elastic; ultra-soft bed gels (0.1 MPa) have low cohesive strength (~0.1-0.3 MPa), and a skin puncture exposes the bed. Dimensionless: modulus ratio skin/bed 50, shear-lag length/base radius 0.32, xi_b 0.875. Simulation coefficient: areal compliance 1.053e-8 m/Pa (informational).
